nodes.name: Cognitive radio
nodes.statement: A {\em cognitive radio} (CR) is a frequency-agile wireless communication device with a monitoring interface and intelligent decision-making that enables dynamic spectrum access~\cite{Zhao07c}.
differentia: with a monitoring interface and intelligent decision-making that enables dynamic spectrum access

nodes.name: Primary and secondary users
nodes.statement: The CR concept represents a significant paradigm change in spectrum regulation and utilization, i.e., from exclusive use of spectrum by licensed users (or, {\em primary users}) to dynamic spectrum access for unlicensed users (or, {\em secondary users}).

nodes.name: False alarm and miss detection
nodes.statement: It has been shown in prior work that generally there are two types of channel sensing errors: (i) {\em false alarm}, when an idle channel is identified as busy, thus a spectrum opportunity will be wasted, (ii) {\em miss detection}, when a busy channel is identified as idle, thus leading to collision with primary users, since CR users will attempt to use such ``idle'' channels.
nodes.statement_short: False alarm: idle channel sensed busy; miss detection: busy channel sensed idle.

nodes.name: Synchronous slot structure of primary users
nodes.statement: We assume the primary users access the channels following a synchronous slot structure as in prior work~\cite{Zhao07c, Su08JNL, Hu09}.

nodes.name: Independent two-state Markov channels
nodes.statement: The channel states are independent to each other and each of the $M$ channels evolves over time following a discrete-time two-state Markov process, as shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:ChanModel}.

nodes.name: Network state vector
nodes.statement: We define the {\em network state vector} in slot $t$ as $\vec{S}(t)=[S_1(t),S_2(t),\dots,S_M(t)]$, where $S_m(t)$ denotes the state of channel $m$, for $m=1, 2, \cdots, M$.

nodes.name: Channel state encoding
nodes.statement: When channel $m$ is idle, we have $S_m(t)=0$; when channel $m$ is busy, we have $S_m(t)=1$.

nodes.name: Channel transition probabilities
nodes.statement: Let $\lambda_m$ and $\mu_m$ be the transition probability of remaining in state $0$ and the transition probability from state $1$ to $0$ for channel $m$, respectively.

nodes.name: Channel utilization
nodes.statement: Let $\eta_m = \Pr(S_m=1)$ denote the {\em utilization} of channel $m$ with respect to primary user transmissions.

nodes.name: Channel idle probability
nodes.statement: Let $\zeta_m = \Pr(S_m=0)$ be the probability that channel $m$ is idle (i.e., not being used by primary users).

nodes.name: Stationary busy probability of channel m
nodes.statement: \eta_m & = & \lim_{T\to \infty} \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T S_m(t) = \frac{1-\lambda_m}{1-\lambda_m+\mu_m}
nodes.label: eq:ProbBusy

nodes.name: Stationary idle probability of channel m
nodes.statement: \zeta_m & = & 1 - \Pr(S_m=1) = \frac{\mu_m}{1 - \lambda_m + \mu_m}.
nodes.label: eq:ProbIdle

nodes.name: Collocated secondary network with N users
nodes.statement: We assume a secondary network collocated with the $M$ primary networks, within which $N$ secondary users take advantage of the spectrum white spaces in $M$ licensed channels for data transmissions.

nodes.name: Two transceivers per secondary user
nodes.statement: As in prior work~\cite{Su08JNL, Nan07, Motamedi07}, we assume that each secondary user is equipped with two transceivers: a {\em control transceiver} that operates over a dedicated control channel, which we assume is always available (e.g., a channel in the industrial, scientific and medical (ISM) band), and a {\em data transceiver} that is used for data communications through the $M$ licensed channels.

nodes.name: Sensing phase and transmission phase
nodes.statement: The time slot structure of the proposed MAC protocols is shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:SlotStructure}, which consists of a {\em sensing phase} and a {\em transmission phase}.
nodes.section: 3 Sensing Error Aware CR MAC Protocol

nodes.name: Mini-slots of the sensing phase
nodes.statement: The sensing phase is further divided into $\bar{K}$ mini-slots, within which each secondary user senses one of the licensed channels.
nodes.section: 3 Sensing Error Aware CR MAC Protocol

nodes.name: Slot, mini-slot and transmission durations
nodes.statement: Let $T_s$, $T_{ms}$, and $T_{data}$ denote the duration of a time slot, a mini-slot, and the transmission phase, respectively (see Fig.~\ref{fig:SlotStructure}), we have \begin{eqnarray} T_s = \bar{K} \times T_{ms} + T_{data}. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.section: 3 Sensing Error Aware CR MAC Protocol

nodes.name: Time slot duration
nodes.statement: T_s = \bar{K} \times T_{ms} + T_{data}.
nodes.section: 3 Sensing Error Aware CR MAC Protocol
nodes.label: eq:ts

nodes.name: Identical detection error probabilities
nodes.statement: We assume all secondary users have the same probability of detection errors when sensing channel $m$, $m=1, 2, \cdots, M$.

nodes.name: False alarm and miss detection probabilities
nodes.statement: Let $\epsilon_m$ and $\delta_m$ denote the probabilities of false alarm and miss detection on channel $m$, respectively.

nodes.name: Sensing result and sensing error probabilities
nodes.statement: For a specific channel $m$ in a certain time slot $t$, the sensing error probabilities can be written as: \begin{eqnarray} && \Pr(W_{m,i}=1 \;|\; S_m=0)=\epsilon_m, \mbox{for all } \; i=1,2,\cdots \\ && \Pr(W_{m,i}=0 \;|\; S_m=1)=\delta_m, \mbox{for all } \; i=1,2,\cdots, \end{eqnarray} where $W_{m,i}$ is the $i$th sensing result of channel $m$ and $S_m$ is state of channel $m$.

nodes.name: Sensing error probabilities
nodes.statement: && \Pr(W_{m,i}=1 \;|\; S_m=0)=\epsilon_m, \mbox{for all } \; i=1,2,\cdots \\ && \Pr(W_{m,i}=0 \;|\; S_m=1)=\delta_m, \mbox{for all } \; i=1,2,\cdots,
nodes.label: eq:ErrorProb

nodes.name: Independent sensing results
nodes.statement: We assume that the sensing results from different users are independent and the sensing results in different mini-slots are also independent to each other.

nodes.name: Conditional channel availability a_{m,k}
nodes.statement_short: Posterior probability that channel $m$ is idle given $k$ independent sensing results, via Bayes' rule with likelihood ratios $\alpha_m,\beta_m$.

nodes.name: Bayesian channel availability formula
nodes.label: eq:AvailProb

nodes.name: Likelihood ratio alpha_m
nodes.statement: \alpha_m = \frac{\Pr(W_{m,i}=0 | S_m=1)}{\Pr(W_{m,i}=0 | S_m=0)}=\frac{\delta_m}{1-\epsilon_m}, \; \mbox{for } \theta_{m,i}=0

nodes.name: Likelihood ratio beta_m
nodes.statement: \beta_m = \frac{\Pr(W_{m,i}=1 | S_m=1)}{\Pr(W_{m,i}=1 | S_m=0)}=\frac{1-\delta_m}{\epsilon_m}, \; \mbox{for } \theta_{m,i}=1. \hspace{-0.05in}

nodes.name: Availability with shared sensing results
nodes.statement: For the secondary user, it is also possible that it obtains some of the $k$ sensing results by local measurements, and receives the remaining sensing results from the control channel in the case that some other secondary users are sensing the same channel $m$. By abuse of notation, we also use $a_{m,k}$ to denote the conditional channel availability probability in this case, due to independence of the sensing results.
nodes.statement_short: $a_{m,k}$ also applies when some of the $k$ results come from other users, by independence.

nodes.name: Monotonicity of channel availability in k
nodes.statement: When channel $m$ is idle, $a_{m,k}$ is a monotone increasing function of $k$; when channel $m$ is busy, $a_{m,k}$ is a monotone decreasing function of $k$.
conclusions: $a_{m,k}$ is a monotone increasing function of $k$
$a_{m,k}$ is a monotone decreasing function of $k$

nodes.name: Sign of log terms and idle bias
nodes.statement: Since $\epsilon_m <0.5$ and $\delta_m<0.5$ for practical sensors, both $\log \left( \frac{1-\delta_m}{\epsilon_m} \right)$ and $\log \left( \frac{1-\epsilon_m}{\delta_m} \right)$ are positive. If $S_m(t)=0$, we have that $\Pr(W_{i,k+1}=1)<\Pr(W_{i,k+1}=0)=\Pr(\bar{W}_{i,k+1}=1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Both log coefficients are positive; when idle, a 0 result is more likely than 1.

nodes.name: Conclude monotonicity
nodes.statement: It follows that $\Pr(a_{m,k}\ge\theta_1) < \Pr(a_{m,k+1}\ge\theta_1)$. That is, $a_{m,k}$ is a monotone increasing function of $k$. Similarly, we can show that $\Pr(a_{m,k}\le\theta_0) < \Pr(a_{m,k+1}\le\theta_0)$ when $S_m(t)=1$. That is, $a_{m,k}$ is a monotone decreasing function of $k$ when the channel is busy.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude increasing in $k$ when idle; the busy case is symmetric.

nodes.name: Threshold-based channel decision rule
nodes.statement: During the sensing phase, each secondary user chooses one channel to sense with equal probability at the beginning of the time slot. Secondary users also report their sensing results over the control channel, and share the corresponding channel sensing results during the mini-slots. Two threshold probabilities $\Theta_0 < \Theta_1$ are used for decision making. \begin{itemize} \item If the availability of channel $m$, i.e., $a_{m,k}$, is below $\Theta_0$, the channel is believed to be busy and the secondary users will wait till the next time slot to start sensing again. \item If the availability of channel $m$ is between $\Theta_0$ and $\Theta_1$, secondary users will keep on sensing the same channel to obtain more sensing results for more accurate estimation of the channel state, until the maximum number of mini-slots, $\bar{K}$, is reached. \item If the availability of channel $m$ exceeds $\Theta_1$, the channel is believed to be idle and the secondary users stop sensing and prepare to access the channel (see Section~\ref{subsec:transph}). \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Users sense a random channel, share results, and per mini-slot declare it busy below $\Theta_0$, idle above $\Theta_1$, or keep sensing until $\bar{K}$.

nodes.name: Choose channel to sense
nodes.statement: During the sensing phase, each secondary user chooses one channel to sense with equal probability at the beginning of the time slot.

nodes.name: Share sensing results
nodes.statement: Secondary users also report their sensing results over the control channel, and share the corresponding channel sensing results during the mini-slots.

nodes.name: Declare busy below Theta_0
nodes.statement: If the availability of channel $m$, i.e., $a_{m,k}$, is below $\Theta_0$, the channel is believed to be busy and the secondary users will wait till the next time slot to start sensing again.

nodes.name: Keep sensing between thresholds
nodes.statement: If the availability of channel $m$ is between $\Theta_0$ and $\Theta_1$, secondary users will keep on sensing the same channel to obtain more sensing results for more accurate estimation of the channel state, until the maximum number of mini-slots, $\bar{K}$, is reached.

nodes.name: Declare idle above Theta_1
nodes.statement: If the availability of channel $m$ exceeds $\Theta_1$, the channel is believed to be idle and the secondary users stop sensing and prepare to access the channel (see Section~\ref{subsec:transph}).

nodes.name: Stop time K_m
nodes.statement: The {\em stop time} $K_m$ when secondary users stop sensing channel $m$, is a random variable that takes value between $1$ and $\bar{K}$, the maximum number of mini-slots that can be used for sensing (see Fig.~\ref{fig:SlotStructure}).

nodes.name: Unidentified channels are not accessed
nodes.statement: If we have $\Theta_0 < a_{m,k} < \Theta_1$ by the end of the sensing phase, then channel $m$ state is not identified due to lack of time (or sensing results) and the channel will not be accessed.

nodes.name: Estimate sets Psi^0, Psi^1, Psi^2
nodes.statement: When there are $k$ sensing results available (e.g., one user senses channel $m$ for $k$ mini-slots, or it senses channel $m$ for less than $k$ mini-slots and receives some channel $m$ sensing results from other secondary users), we define three sets of estimates for the state of channel $m$, as: \begin{eqnarray} \Psi^0_{m,k}&=&\{d_m\;|\;a_{m,k}\le \Theta_0, \forall \; 0 \le d_m \le k\} \\ \Psi^1_{m,k}&=&\{d_m\;|\;a_{m,k}\ge \Theta_1, \forall \; 0 \le d_m \le k\} \\ \Psi^2_{m,k}&=& \{d_m\;|\;\Theta_0 < a_{m,k} < \Theta_1, \forall \; 0 \le d_m \le k\} = \overline{(\Psi^0_{m,k} \cup \Psi^1_{m,k})}, \end{eqnarray} where $d_m$ is the number of observations whose sensing result is $0$ on channel $m$.
nodes.statement_short: Sets of zero-counts $d_m$ for which $a_{m,k}$ is below $\Theta_0$, above $\Theta_1$, or in between.

nodes.name: Busy estimate set
nodes.statement: \Psi^0_{m,k}&=&\{d_m\;|\;a_{m,k}\le \Theta_0, \forall \; 0 \le d_m \le k\}
nodes.label: eq:Psi0

nodes.name: Idle estimate set
nodes.statement: \Psi^1_{m,k}&=&\{d_m\;|\;a_{m,k}\ge \Theta_1, \forall \; 0 \le d_m \le k\}
nodes.label: eq:Psi1

nodes.name: Undecided estimate set
nodes.statement: \Psi^2_{m,k}&=& \{d_m\;|\;\Theta_0 < a_{m,k} < \Theta_1, \forall \; 0 \le d_m \le k\} = \overline{(\Psi^0_{m,k} \cup \Psi^1_{m,k})},
nodes.label: eq:Psi2

nodes.name: Memoryless sensing policy
nodes.statement: We call the policy ``memoryless'' since it does not consider the channel sensing and access results in the previous time slot for simplicity. With this memoryless policy, each secondary user chooses one of the $M$ licensed channels to sense with equal probability, i.e., $1/M$. Furthermore, channel selections of the $N$ secondary users are independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.).
nodes.statement_short: Each secondary user independently picks one of the $M$ channels uniformly at random to sense, ignoring past slots.
also_stated_at: With the {\em memoryless sensing} policy, each secondary user chooses one of the $M$ licensed channels to sense with equal probability.

nodes.name: Number of users sensing channel m
nodes.statement: Let $U_m$ be the random variable representing the number of secondary users that select channel $m$ to sense.

nodes.name: Binomial distribution of users per channel
nodes.statement: \Pr(U_m=u_m)=\left(\!\!\! \begin{array}{c} N \\ u_m \end{array} \!\!\!\right) \left( \frac{1}{M} \right)^{u_m} \left( \frac{M-1}{M} \right)^{N-u_m}_{.}
nodes.label: eq:NumUser

nodes.name: Joint distribution of users over channels
nodes.statement: \Pr(u_1, u_2, \cdots, u_M) = \left\{ \begin{array}{ll} \prod_{m=1}^M \Pr(U_m=u_m), & \mbox{if } \; \sum_{m=1}^M u_m=N \\ 0, & \mbox{otherwise}. \end{array} \right.
nodes.label: eq:JtNumUser

nodes.name: Interpretation of the stop time
nodes.statement: The stop time $K_m < \bar{K}$ has two implications. First, it means that secondary users stop sensing channel $m$ after mini-slot $K_m$. Second, it indicates that the estimated availability of channel $m$, $a_{m,k}$, has already exceeded the threshold $\Theta_1$. Thus these secondary users think channel $m$ is idle and are ready to access the channel for data transmission. Note that a secondary user also stops sensing a channel $m$ when $a_{m,k} < \Theta_0$ (when it is sure that the channel is busy). We are not interested in this case, since the secondary user will back off until the next time slot. Thus $K_m$ is defined with regard to the event $a_{m,k} > \Theta_1$.
nodes.statement_short: $K_m<\bar{K}$ means sensing stopped because availability exceeded $\Theta_1$; $K_m$ is defined only w.r.t. that event.

nodes.name: Probability of stop time 1
nodes.statement: We first derive the conditional probability for event $K_m=1$, as \begin{eqnarray} && \Pr(K_m=1 \; | \; U_m=u \;, \;S_m=0) = \Pr(a_{m,u} \ge \Theta_1) \nonumber \\ & = & \sum_{d_m^1 \in \Psi^1_{m,u}} \left(\!\!\! \begin{array}{c} u \\ d_m^1 \end{array} \!\!\!\right)\left[ (\epsilon_m)^{u-d_m^1}(1-\epsilon_m)^{d_m^1} \right], \end{eqnarray} where $d_m^1$ is the number of observations whose sensing result is $0$ in the first mini-slot.
nodes.statement_short: Probability sensing stops at mini-slot 1 given $u$ users and idle channel, summing binomial terms over $\Psi^1_{m,u}$.

nodes.name: Conditional probability of stopping at K_m=1
nodes.statement: && \Pr(K_m=1 \; | \; U_m=u \;, \;S_m=0) = \Pr(a_{m,u} \ge \Theta_1) \nonumber \\ & = & \sum_{d_m^1 \in \Psi^1_{m,u}} \left(\!\!\! \begin{array}{c} u \\ d_m^1 \end{array} \!\!\!\right)\left[ (\epsilon_m)^{u-d_m^1}(1-\epsilon_m)^{d_m^1} \right],
nodes.label: eq:CondStop1

nodes.name: Probability of stop time 2
nodes.statement: Following similar reasoning as in (\ref{eq:CondStop1}), we can obtain the conditional probability for the event that the stop time $K_m=2$ as \begin{eqnarray} && \Pr(K_m=2 \; | \; U_m=u \;, \;S_m=0) = \Pr \left[(\Theta_0 < a_{m,u} < \Theta_1) \cap (a_{m,2u} \ge \Theta_1) \right] \nonumber \\ & = & \hspace*{-0.1in} \sum_{D_m^2 \in \Psi^1_{m,2u}}\sum_{d_m^1 \in \Psi^2_{m,u}} \hspace*{-0.1in} \left(\!\!\! \begin{array}{c} u \\ d_m^1 \end{array} \!\!\!\right) \left(\!\!\! \begin{array}{c} u \\ d_m^2 \end{array} \!\!\!\right) \left[(\epsilon_m)^{2u-D_m^2} (1-\epsilon_m)^{D_m^2}\right], \end{eqnarray} where $\Psi^{2}_{m,k}$ is defined in (\ref{eq:Psi2}) and $D_m^2=d_m^1 + d_m^2$.

nodes.name: Conditional probability of stopping at K_m=2
nodes.statement: && \Pr(K_m=2 \; | \; U_m=u \;, \;S_m=0) = \Pr \left[(\Theta_0 < a_{m,u} < \Theta_1) \cap (a_{m,2u} \ge \Theta_1) \right] \nonumber \\ & = & \hspace*{-0.1in} \sum_{D_m^2 \in \Psi^1_{m,2u}}\sum_{d_m^1 \in \Psi^2_{m,u}} \hspace*{-0.1in} \left(\!\!\! \begin{array}{c} u \\ d_m^1 \end{array} \!\!\!\right) \left(\!\!\! \begin{array}{c} u \\ d_m^2 \end{array} \!\!\!\right) \left[(\epsilon_m)^{2u-D_m^2} (1-\epsilon_m)^{D_m^2}\right],

nodes.name: Probability of stop time k
nodes.statement: In the general case, we can derive the conditional probability for the event that the stop time is $K_m=k$ as: \begin{eqnarray} & & \hspace*{-0.1in} \Pr(K_m=k \; | \; U_m=u\; , \; S_m=0) \nonumber \\ & & \hspace*{-0.25in} = \Pr \left[(\Theta_0 < a_{m,u} < \Theta_1)\cap (\Theta_0 < a_{m,2u} < \Theta_1) \cap \cdots \cap (\Theta_0 < a_{m,(k-1)u} < \Theta_1) \cap (a_{m,ku}\ge \Theta_1) \right] \nonumber \\ & & \hspace*{-0.25in} = \sum_{D_m^k \in \Psi^1_{m,ku}} \sum_{D_m^{k-1} \in \Psi^2_{m,(k-1)u}}\cdots \sum_{d_m^1 \in \Psi^2_{m,u}} \left(\!\!\! \begin{array}{c} u \\ d_m^1 \end{array} \!\!\!\right) \left(\!\!\! \begin{array}{c} u \\ d_m^2 \end{array} \!\!\!\right) \cdots \left(\!\!\! \begin{array}{c} u \\ d_m^k \end{array} \!\!\!\right) \left[ (\epsilon_m)^{ku-D_m^k}(1-\epsilon_m)^{D_m^k} \right], \end{eqnarray} where $k = 1, \cdots, \bar{K}$ and $D_m^k=\sum_{i=1}^k d_m^i$.
nodes.statement_short: General stop-time distribution: undecided for $k-1$ mini-slots, then above $\Theta_1$, given $u$ users and idle channel.

nodes.name: Conditional probability of stopping at K_m=k
nodes.statement: & & \hspace*{-0.1in} \Pr(K_m=k \; | \; U_m=u\; , \; S_m=0) \nonumber \\ & & \hspace*{-0.25in} = \Pr \left[(\Theta_0 < a_{m,u} < \Theta_1)\cap (\Theta_0 < a_{m,2u} < \Theta_1) \cap \cdots \cap (\Theta_0 < a_{m,(k-1)u} < \Theta_1) \cap (a_{m,ku}\ge \Theta_1) \right] \nonumber \\ & & \hspace*{-0.25in} = \sum_{D_m^k \in \Psi^1_{m,ku}} \sum_{D_m^{k-1} \in \Psi^2_{m,(k-1)u}}\cdots \sum_{d_m^1 \in \Psi^2_{m,u}} \left(\!\!\! \begin{array}{c} u \\ d_m^1 \end{array} \!\!\!\right) \left(\!\!\! \begin{array}{c} u \\ d_m^2 \end{array} \!\!\!\right) \cdots \left(\!\!\! \begin{array}{c} u \\ d_m^k \end{array} \!\!\!\right) \left[ (\epsilon_m)^{ku-D_m^k}(1-\epsilon_m)^{D_m^k} \right],
nodes.label: eq:CondStopk

nodes.name: Probability a channel is unsensed under memoryless policy
nodes.statement: Under the memoryless sensing policy, some channels may not be sensed by any of the secondary users. Such an event occurs with probability $\Pr (U_m=0) = \left( \frac{M-1}{M} \right)^N $, which is sufficiently large when $M$ is large and/or the number of secondary users is close to the number of channels.
conclusions: Such an event occurs with probability $\Pr (U_m=0) = \left( \frac{M-1}{M} \right)^N $

nodes.name: Improved sensing policy
nodes.statement: The improved sensing policy incorporates a mechanism to spread secondary users to the channels. It also exploits channel state autocorrelation by considering sensing results and channel states in the previous time slot. By the end of the sensing phase in a time slot $t$, the secondary users compute the channel availability $a_{m,k}$ for each channel $m$. During the following transmission phase, if a secondary user transmits on channel $m$, it can obtain more accurate channel state information: if its transmission is successful, then channel $m$ is idle in time slot $t$; otherwise, channel $m$ is busy in the time slot. Such channel information can be exchanged at the beginning of the sensing phase in the next time slot. Then, we can classify the $M$ channels into three sets according to the channel states in time slot $t$, including \begin{itemize} \item The set of channels that are detected or believed to be idle, denoted by $\mathcal{B}_0(t)$. \item The set of channels that are detected or believed to be busy, denoted by $\mathcal{B}_1(t)$. \item The set of channels whose states are not identified due to lack of time or not sensed by any of the secondary users, denoted by $\mathcal{B}_2(t)$. \end{itemize} Let $|\mathcal{B}_0(t)|$, $|\mathcal{B}_1(t)|$ and $|\mathcal{B}_2(t)|$ be the cardinalities of $\mathcal{B}_0(t)$, $\mathcal{B}_1(t)$, and $\mathcal{B}_2(t)$, respectively. If channel $m$ is in set $\mathcal{B}_0(t)$ and the stop time on channel $m$ is less than the maximum stop time $\bar{K}$, one user among those $u_m$ users that are sensing this channel will be randomly chosen to switch to sense another channel in the set $m \cup \mathcal{B}_1(t) \cup \mathcal{B}_2(t)$ in time slot $(t+1)$. If channel $m$ is in set $\mathcal{B}_1(t)$ and the stop time on channel $m$ is less than the maximum stop time $\bar{K}$, the secondary users that are sensing this channel will randomly choose a channel in $m \cup \mathcal{B}_2(t)$ to sense in time slot $(t+1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Use last slot's sensing and transmission outcomes to classify channels idle/busy/unknown and reassign users toward busy or unknown channels. Spreads users (load balancing) and exploits channel autocorrelation.

nodes.name: Compute channel availabilities
nodes.statement: By the end of the sensing phase in a time slot $t$, the secondary users compute the channel availability $a_{m,k}$ for each channel $m$.

nodes.name: Learn state from transmission outcome
nodes.statement: During the following transmission phase, if a secondary user transmits on channel $m$, it can obtain more accurate channel state information: if its transmission is successful, then channel $m$ is idle in time slot $t$; otherwise, channel $m$ is busy in the time slot.

nodes.name: Exchange channel information
nodes.statement: Such channel information can be exchanged at the beginning of the sensing phase in the next time slot.

nodes.name: Classify channels into three sets
nodes.statement: Then, we can classify the $M$ channels into three sets according to the channel states in time slot $t$, including \begin{itemize} \item The set of channels that are detected or believed to be idle, denoted by $\mathcal{B}_0(t)$. \item The set of channels that are detected or believed to be busy, denoted by $\mathcal{B}_1(t)$. \item The set of channels whose states are not identified due to lack of time or not sensed by any of the secondary users, denoted by $\mathcal{B}_2(t)$. \end{itemize}

nodes.name: Reassign one user from idle channel
nodes.statement: If channel $m$ is in set $\mathcal{B}_0(t)$ and the stop time on channel $m$ is less than the maximum stop time $\bar{K}$, one user among those $u_m$ users that are sensing this channel will be randomly chosen to switch to sense another channel in the set $m \cup \mathcal{B}_1(t) \cup \mathcal{B}_2(t)$ in time slot $(t+1)$.

nodes.name: Reassign users from busy channel
nodes.statement: If channel $m$ is in set $\mathcal{B}_1(t)$ and the stop time on channel $m$ is less than the maximum stop time $\bar{K}$, the secondary users that are sensing this channel will randomly choose a channel in $m \cup \mathcal{B}_2(t)$ to sense in time slot $(t+1)$.

nodes.name: Load balancing effect of improved sensing
nodes.statement: With the above mechanism that reassigns secondary users to channels based on the sensing results in the previous time slot, we can reduce the chance that a licensed channel is not sensed by any of the users. This approach achieves the {\em load balancing} effect since it attempts to spread out secondary users to the channels.

nodes.name: p-persistent CSMA
nodes.statement: We adopt the $p$-persistent CSMA protocol for data channel access for secondary users during the data transmission phase. Under this protocol, a secondary user delays its transmission when the channels are busy. Once one or more channels are detected idle, the secondary user will attempt to access the idle channel(s) for data transmission with probability $p$.
nodes.statement_short: Defer while channels are busy; once a channel is idle, transmit on it with probability $p$.

nodes.name: Defer when busy
nodes.statement: Under this protocol, a secondary user delays its transmission when the channels are busy.

nodes.name: Access idle channel with probability p
nodes.statement: Once one or more channels are detected idle, the secondary user will attempt to access the idle channel(s) for data transmission with probability $p$.

nodes.name: Heavy load
nodes.statement: We consider the heavy load domain, where each secondary user always has data to send to every other secondary user.

nodes.name: Case 1 per-channel access
nodes.statement: Once the estimate of channel $m$, i.e., $a_{m,k}$, exceeds threshold $\Theta_1$, each of the secondary users sensing channel $m$ will send an RTS packet on channel $m$ with probability $p$, to contend for the transmission opportunity on this channel. If there is only one secondary user that sends RTS, then it wins the channel; if there is no secondary user that sends RTS, then the channel will not be accessed and will be wasted; if there are more than one RTS packets sent on channel $m$, there is collision and none of the secondary users can use the channel.
nodes.statement_short: Users sensing channel $m$ send RTS on it with probability $p$ once $a_{m,k}>\Theta_1$; exactly one RTS wins the channel.

nodes.name: Send RTS with probability p
nodes.statement: Once the estimate of channel $m$, i.e., $a_{m,k}$, exceeds threshold $\Theta_1$, each of the secondary users sensing channel $m$ will send an RTS packet on channel $m$ with probability $p$, to contend for the transmission opportunity on this channel.

nodes.name: Resolve contention
nodes.statement: If there is only one secondary user that sends RTS, then it wins the channel; if there is no secondary user that sends RTS, then the channel will not be accessed and will be wasted; if there are more than one RTS packets sent on channel $m$, there is collision and none of the secondary users can use the channel.

nodes.name: Per-channel RTS idle/success/collision probabilities
nodes.statement: We define $P_m^{idle}$, $P_m^{succ}$ and $P_m^{coll}$ as the probability that there is no RTS transmission on channel $m$, the probability that exactly one secondary user successfully transmits an RTS on channel $m$, and the probability that there is collision on channel $m$ when multiple RTS packets are transmitted, respectively.

nodes.name: Per-channel access probabilities under p-persistent CSMA
nodes.statement: && \hspace*{-0.4in} P_m^{idle}(U_m) = (1-p)^{U_m} \\ && \hspace*{-0.4in} P_m^{succ}(U_m) = U_m\times p\times(1-p)^{U_m-1} \\ && \hspace*{-0.4in} P_m^{coll}(U_m) = 1 - P_m^{idle}(U_m) - P_m^{succ}(U_m) = 1-(1-p)^{U_m}-U_m\times p\times(1-p)^{U_m-1}_{.}
nodes.label: eq:ProbAccess

nodes.name: Channel bonding
nodes.statement: We assume that the CR users can transmit data over more than one channels using the channel bonding/aggregation techniques~\cite{Su08JNL, Corderio06}.

nodes.name: Case 2 channel-bonding access
nodes.statement: In this case, every secondary user keeps on sensing the channel until the channel state is identified or until the end of the sensing phase. At the beginning of the transmission phase, the set of idle channels are identified and are know to all the secondary users. Then every secondary user will transmit an RTS packet with probability $p$ on the control channel, to contend for the entire set of idle channels. If there is only one secondary user that sends RTS on the control channel, it wins the entire set of idle channels. Otherwise, the idle channels will be wasted (i.e., when no RTS is sent, or more than one RTS are sent on the control channel).
nodes.statement_short: All users sense to the end of the sensing phase, then contend with RTS on the control channel; a single winner takes all idle channels.

nodes.name: Sense until identified or phase ends
nodes.statement: In this case, every secondary user keeps on sensing the channel until the channel state is identified or until the end of the sensing phase.

nodes.name: Identify idle channels
nodes.statement: At the beginning of the transmission phase, the set of idle channels are identified and are know to all the secondary users.

nodes.name: Contend on control channel
nodes.statement: Then every secondary user will transmit an RTS packet with probability $p$ on the control channel, to contend for the entire set of idle channels.

nodes.name: Resolve contention
nodes.statement: If there is only one secondary user that sends RTS on the control channel, it wins the entire set of idle channels. Otherwise, the idle channels will be wasted (i.e., when no RTS is sent, or more than one RTS are sent on the control channel).

nodes.name: Control-channel RTS idle/success/collision probabilities
nodes.statement: We define $P^{idle}$, $P^{succ}$ and $P^{coll}$ as the probability of no RTS transmission on the control channel, the probability that exactly one RTS sent on the control channel, and the probability of collision on the control channel, respectively.

nodes.name: Control-channel access probabilities
nodes.statement: && \hspace*{-0.4in} P^{idle}(N) = (1-p)^{N} \\ && \hspace*{-0.4in} P^{succ}(N) = N\times(1-p)^{N-1} \\ && \hspace*{-0.4in} P^{coll}(N) = 1 - P^{idle}(N) - P^{succ}(N) = 1-(1-p)^{N}-N\times p \times (1-p)^{N-1}_{.}
nodes.label: eq:ProbAccess2

nodes.name: Maximum tolerable collision probability
nodes.statement: Let $\gamma_m \in [0,1]$ be the maximum tolerable collision probability to primary users on channel $m$: $\gamma_m=0$ means that no secondary transmission is allowed, while $\gamma_m=1$ means that secondary users have the same privilege as primary users when accessing the channels.

nodes.name: Conditional miss-detection stop probability
nodes.statement: & & \hspace*{-0.2in} \Pr(K_m=k \; | \; U_m=u,S_m=1) \nonumber \\ & & \hspace*{-0.4in} = \sum_{D_m^k \in \Psi^1_{m,ku}} \sum_{D_m^{k-1} \in \Psi^2_{m,(k-1)u}}\cdots \sum_{d_m^1 \in \Psi^2_{m,u}} \left(\!\!\! \begin{array}{c} u \\ d_m^1 \end{array} \!\!\!\right) \left(\!\!\! \begin{array}{c} u \\ d_m^2 \end{array} \!\!\!\right) \cdots \left(\!\!\! \begin{array}{c} u \\ d_m^k \end{array} \!\!\!\right)(\delta_m)^{D_m^k}(1-\delta_m)^{ku-D_m^k}_{.}
nodes.label: eq:CondIntf

nodes.name: Interference probability in Case 1
nodes.statement: P_{m,1}^{intf} = \sum_{k=1}^{\bar{K}}\sum_{u=0}^N \Pr(K_m=k \; | \; U_m=u,S_m=1) \times \Pr(U_m=u) \times \left[ P_m^{succ}(u)+P_m^{coll}(u) \right].
nodes.label: eq:ProbIntf

nodes.name: Interference probability in Case 2
nodes.statement: P_{m,2}^{intf} = \sum_{k=1}^{\bar{K}}\sum_{u=0}^N \Pr(K_m=k \; | \; U_m=u,S_m=1) \times \Pr(U_m=u) \times P^{succ}(N).
nodes.label: eq:ProbIntf2

nodes.name: Primary user protection constraint
nodes.statement: For primary user protection, the probability of secndary users causing collision with primary users on channel $m$ should be kept lower than or equal to $\gamma_m$, i.e., \begin{eqnarray} P_m^{intf} \le \gamma_m. \end{eqnarray}
also_stated_at: For protection of primary users, the probability of collision caused by secondary user transmissions to primary users should be upper bounded by a prescribed threshold $\gamma_m$, for $m=1,2,\cdots,M$.
The probability of collision caused by secondary users to primary users should be kept below $\gamma_m$.

nodes.name: Interference constraint
nodes.statement: P_m^{intf} \le \gamma_m.

nodes.name: Ignore RTS/CTS overhead
nodes.statement: Without loss of generality, we ignore the time spent on RTS/CTS exchanges, which can be approximated by a fixed amount of overhead.

nodes.name: Case 1 per-channel throughput
nodes.statement: In Case 1, the expected throughput of channel $m$ that is sensed by $u$ users, denoted by $\Lambda^1_m(u)$, can be derived as \begin{eqnarray} \Lambda^1_m(u) = \sum_{k=1}^{\bar{K}}\Pr(K_m=k\; | \; U_m=u,S_m=0) \times R_m \times \frac{1}{T_s} \times \left[ (\bar{K}-k) T_{ms} + T_{data} \right], \end{eqnarray} where $R_m$ is the data rate of channel $m$, and $T_s$ is the time slot duration given in (\ref{eq:ts}).

nodes.name: Case 1 per-channel throughput formula
nodes.statement: \Lambda^1_m(u) = \sum_{k=1}^{\bar{K}}\Pr(K_m=k\; | \; U_m=u,S_m=0) \times R_m \times \frac{1}{T_s} \times \left[ (\bar{K}-k) T_{ms} + T_{data} \right],

nodes.name: Sensing state vector
nodes.statement: Let $\vec{U}=[U_1, U_2, \cdots, U_M]$ denote the secondary user {\em sensing state vector}, where each element $U_m$ represents the number of secondary users that choose channel $m$ to sense and access.

nodes.name: Case 1 aggregate throughput
nodes.statement: The aggregate throughput for the CR network, denoted by $\Omega_1$, is \begin{eqnarray} \Omega_1 = \sum_{\vec{U}} \Pr(\vec{U}) \sum_{\vec{S}} \Pr(\vec{S}) \sum_{m=1}^M \left( I_{[S_m=0]}\Lambda^1_m(u) \times P_m^{succ}(u) \right), \end{eqnarray} where $\vec{S}$ is the channel state vector defined in Section~\ref{sec:model}, $P_m^{succ}(u)$ is given in (\ref{eq:pmsucc}) and $I_{[S_m=0]}$ is an indicator that channel $m$ is idle, i.e., \begin{equation} I_{[S_m=0]} = \left\{ \begin{array}{ll} 1, & \mbox{if } S_m=0 \\ 0, & \mbox{otherwise}. \end{array} \right. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Network throughput in Case 1: expectation over sensing and channel states of per-channel throughput times RTS success probability.

nodes.name: Case 1 aggregate throughput formula
nodes.statement: \Omega_1 = \sum_{\vec{U}} \Pr(\vec{U}) \sum_{\vec{S}} \Pr(\vec{S}) \sum_{m=1}^M \left( I_{[S_m=0]}\Lambda^1_m(u) \times P_m^{succ}(u) \right),

nodes.name: Idle indicator
nodes.statement: I_{[S_m=0]} = \left\{ \begin{array}{ll} 1, & \mbox{if } S_m=0 \\ 0, & \mbox{otherwise}. \end{array} \right.

nodes.name: Early stopping versus waiting in Cases 1 and 2
nodes.statement: In Case 1, the sensing process on channel $m$ can stop early if the estimate of channel availability $a_{m,k}$ exceeds threshold $\Theta_1$ or drops below the threshold $\Theta_0$. In the former case, the remaining mini-slots can be used to transmit data. In Case 2, all CR users wait till the beginning of the transmission phase, and then contend for the idle channels by sending RTS packets on the control channel. The winning secondary user's data transmissions start at the beginning of the transmission phase (i.e., after $\bar{K}$ mini-slots).
nodes.statement_short: Case 1 can use leftover mini-slots for data after early stopping; Case 2 always starts data after $\bar{K}$ mini-slots.

nodes.name: Case 2 per-channel throughput
nodes.statement: \Lambda^2_m(u) = \sum_{k=1}^{\bar{K}}\Pr(K_m=k\; | \; U_m=u,S_m=0) \times R_m \times \frac{T_{data}}{T_s},

nodes.name: Case 2 aggregate throughput
nodes.statement: \Omega_2=\sum_{\vec{U}} \Pr(\vec{U}) \sum_{\vec{S}} \Pr(\vec{S}) \sum_{m=1}^M \left( I_{[S_m=0]}\Lambda^2_m(u) P^{succ}(N) \right).

nodes.name: Random sensing scheme
nodes.statement: A simple random sensing scheme that each user chooses one channel to sense with equal probability, termed {\em Random} in the plots.

nodes.name: Negotiation-based sensing policy (NSP)
nodes.statement: With this scheme, different secondary users attempt to select distinct channels to sense by overhearing the control packets on the control channel~\cite{Su08JNL}.

nodes.name: Analysis is exact for memoryless sensing
nodes.statement: We observe that the simulation and analysis curves for the memoryless sensing CR MACs overlap completely with each other, indicating that our analysis is exact.

nodes.name: Analysis upper-bounds improved-sensing throughput
nodes.statement: We find the analysis can serve as a tight upper bound for the CR MAC throughput performance when the improved sensing policy is incorporated.
conclusions: the analysis can serve as a tight upper bound for the CR MAC throughput performance

nodes.name: Throughput gain of improved sensing
nodes.statement: The improved sensing MAC achieves the best performance, with about 10\% gain over the memoryless sensing MAC and about 200\% gain over the two existing approaches.
conclusions: The improved sensing MAC achieves the best performance

nodes.name: Proposed schemes respect collision threshold
nodes.statement: On the other hand, the collision probabilities of the proposed schemes are kept around 2.5\% for the entire range of $\eta$ examined.
conclusions: the collision probabilities of the proposed schemes are kept around 2.5\%
